    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Recent findings suggest that dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio noted. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Bessent stated in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    Sources indicate that after years of overspending, Dalio noted total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    According to recent reports, to solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    First, Dalio remarked the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Latest York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio noted. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    According to recent reports, dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    • Spousal Social Security checks tend to be a lot smaller than retirement benefits, averaging just $988 in October 2026 compared to $2,092 for retirement checks.
    • Sources indicate that spousal benefits have a few rules that make them different from retirement benefits, and it's important to understand them if you proposal to apply for these checks next year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00PM EST.

    Spousal Social Security checks tend to be a lot smaller than retirement benefits, averaging just $988 in October 2026 compared to $2,092 for retirement checks. But they can still make a meaningful difference to your household's budget in 2027.

    Sources indicate that spousal benefits have a few rules that make them different from retirement benefits, and it's important to understand them if you proposal to apply for these checks next year. Here are three of the biggest differences you should be aware of.

    It's vital that you and your spouse are both on the same page about when each of you will apply so that you can maximize your household income. If you haven't already talked through your aims, now is a great time to do so before you try to apply for Social Security benefits in 2027.

    Sources indicate that spousal benefits are also available to ex-spouses if you were married to a qualifying worker for at least 10 years before divorcing and you haven’t remarried. Your ex's remarriage will not affect your eligibility to claim benefits on the ex's work record.

    In a recent development, social Security retirement benefits continue to grow for every month you delay your application until you qualify for your maximum checks at age 70. But spousal benefits only grow until you reach your full retirement age (FRA). This is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later.

    #3724. The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • In a recent development, the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    In a recent development, the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    In a recent development, gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    According to recent reports, the Treasury Department remarked last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Sources indicate that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "massive toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Sources indicate that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah noted. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    According to recent reports, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah noted. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    In a recent development, "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah remarked in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares remarked the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh noted in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    In a recent development, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -7.72%) briefly became a $1 trillion tech giant in September, but it lost that milestone after a prolonged artificial intelligence (AI) stock correction. However, the chipmaker is set to rejoin Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) and Apple (AAPL -0.92%) as a trillion-dollar company. These are the catalysts that can drive the stock higher.

    AMD has been viewed as the No. 2 graphics processing unit (GPU) chipmaker for several years, with Nvidia comfortably holding on to the top spot. However, Nvidia suddenly faces significant uncertainty with former CEO Jensen Huang out of the organization and angling for a comeback.

    It has been revealed that nvidia at the moment doesn't seem receptive to a reunion, and that can cost the tech giant. Some investors argue that Huang's departure will make it difficult for Nvidia to continue innovating despite the competitive edge it has already obtained.

    It has been revealed that the AI industry is moving rapidly, and leadership complexities can cost Nvidia valuable time. It can be the difference between missing out on the latest technology and watching hyperscalers turn to alternatives.

    This scenario positions AMD as the chipmaker with the most to gain from the confusion, and the manufacturer has been taking major steps to close the gap. For instance, AMD is making its chip fleet more attractive by making it much easier for developers to port existing Nvidia CUDA applications to its HIP platform.

    It has been revealed that nvidia's CUDA was previously a major moat. Moving to another software essentially meant rewriting vast amounts of code, but that's no longer the case. If AMD can win over more businesses with an easier migration, it creates more headaches for a organization already full of them.

    Industry observers note that although Nvidia has captured most of the headlines throughout the AI boom, AMD has been quietly accelerating its growth. Data center revenue surged by 97% year over year in the third quarter, while overall revenue reached $13.4 billion, up by 45% year over year. That also represents a 16% sequential boost.

    AMD CEO Lisa Su told investors that demand for its AI products is still accelerating. The chipmaker also remains confident that revenue growth will surge in the coming years, along with higher net profit margins.

    AMD trades at a 30 forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which may be higher than what some investors are willing to handle. However, this same tech giant almost doubled its net income year over year. AMD wrapped up the quarter with an 18.2% net profit margin, and if it can get closer to Nvidia's 62% net profit margin, the stock should have an easy time reclaiming a $1 trillion market cap and marching toward new highs.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Burry, the investor made famous by "The Big Short," isn't shy about saying "I told you so.".
    • "Coreweave, Nebius, NVIDIA, semis, I tried to warn you all," Burry posted on X on Thursday afternoon.
    • Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) fell 3.3% on Thursday, CoreWeave (CRWV -6.11%) dropped 6.1%, and Nebius Group (NBIS -9.39%) sank 9.4%, as tech stocks gave up an early rally.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:43PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Michael Burry, the investor made famous by "The Big Short," isn't shy about saying "I told you so.".

    "Coreweave, Nebius, NVIDIA, semis, I tried to warn you all," Burry posted on X on Thursday afternoon. "I didn't say short. But I provided the information one would need to sell.".

    He picked a good day for it. Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) fell 3.3% on Thursday, CoreWeave (CRWV -6.11%) dropped 6.1%, and Nebius Group (NBIS -9.39%) sank 9.4%, as tech stocks gave up an early rally.

    Here's what Burry saw, and what investors should do with it.

    Michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

    Burry's warnings came in pieces. In mid-October, he shared a Wall Street Journal story arguing that CoreWeave's sell-off showed the pressure from rising borrowing costs, adding his own commentary: "Dumb da dumb dumb da.".

    Industry observers note that coreWeave and Nebius are so-called neoclouds, companies that rent out Nvidia-powered computing to AI developers. Building their data centers takes enormous amounts of money, much of it borrowed, so higher interest rates hit them hard.

    In a recent development, on Nvidia, his case is about the long run. He says he expects Nvidia's competitive edge to shrink over the next five years. In September, he also argued that its chips "may be economically depreciating waiting in warehouses while GAAP depreciation remains at zero," meaning the hardware could be losing value faster than the accounting highlights.

    The numbers have lent credence to his concern. CoreWeave closed Thursday at $44.91, down 76% from highs last year, and Nebius finished at $96.92, down 66% from its June peak. Nvidia has held up better but still sits 39% below its October high. The damage has spread across the chip industry, too: The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH -2.62%), a basket of the biggest chip stocks, is down 33% from its June high.

    As he laid out his long-term worries about Nvidia earlier this month, Burry mentioned he imagined "the whole market is going to think this is a heck of a trade fairly soon." But since then, the stock has fallen another 16%.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia's business, meanwhile, hasn't cracked. Its revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and management raised its growth forecast for next year. The stock's slide this month coincided with Jensen Huang's sudden resignation as CEO, rather than a drop in sales.

    In a recent development, if you own neocloud stocks like CoreWeave and Nebius, watch how much they borrow and what that debt costs them. If you own Nvidia, watch whether customers keep buying at today's pace, and whether the chips they buy hold their value.

    Recent findings suggest that the AI stocks that come out of this sell-off in good shape will be the ones with the best answers to those questions. For long-term investors, that's a better guide than any single post on X, even one from Michael Burry.

    Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards speaks on decision to undergo knee surgery, has no clear return timeline: 'Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, then I'll be ready'

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Three weeks after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his ailing knee, Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards is speaking out about his recovery.
    • On Thursday, the guard talked to reporters for the first time since the procedure, saying that the rehabilitation process was "going great" and that he was focused on improving the strength in his leg post-surgery.
    • "It was frustrating, but I realized I had to do it, so I just made my mind up that same day, like we're gonna do it tomorrow," Edwards noted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Three weeks after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his ailing knee, Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards is speaking out about his recovery.

    On Thursday, the guard talked to reporters for the first time since the procedure, saying that the rehabilitation process was "going great" and that he was focused on improving the strength in his leg post-surgery. Edwards also spoke about the timeline of his injury before deciding to go under the knife, saying that his knee had been bothering him on and off for years but that it had "flared up" significantly last month.

    "It was frustrating, but I realized I had to do it, so I just made my mind up that same day, like we're gonna do it tomorrow," Edwards noted.

    The 25-year-old guard said that he had managed his knee well in the offseason and that it was still "good" in camp. But by the Timberwolves' season opener on Oct. 21, it was getting worse, and was "really bothering" him in the team's win over the Orlando Magic on Oct. 23.

    According to recent reports, minnesota's back-to-back on Oct. 25 and Oct. 26, against the Toronto Raptors at home and the Cleveland Cavaliers away, is when it really started to be a problem: "After the back-to-back it was really bad, like painful to fly," Edwards said.

    Edwards noted that he hopes that the surgery will help mitigate the pain going forward.

    "It was something that I needed, it needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows, maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else, but hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good.".

    Sources indicate that edwards, who said that this is the longest he's ever gone without playing basketball, added that he looks on coming back this season but doesn't have a clear timeline. At the time of his surgery, reports indicated that he would need more than two months to recover.

    "I have no clue. Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, then I'll be ready," he stated of a return to the court.

    Recent findings suggest that losing Edwards initially seemed to be a brutal blow to the Timberwolves' chances: Before the surgery, Edwards was averaging 33.3 points per game and seemed on track for another dominant season. But Minnesota has fared well in his absence, going 8-3 in the weeks since Edwards' surgery.

    Industry observers note that "I was thirsty to get back, especially after the first game," Edwards said, referring to the Timberwolves' loss to the Golden State Warriors right after his procedure. "I was ready to get back and just get in their ear, tell them what I'm seeing, feel the energy. But after that game, we kinda took off, so I was like, I'll take my time. But I'm happy to be around now.".

    While speaking to reporters, Edwards had high praise for all of his teammates, specifically pointing out the "phenomenal" play of Ayo Dosunmu — who at the moment leads the team in points — and noting that forward Jaden McDaniels is "stepping up big time." He also confirmed that he's been sharing his scouting reports with his teammates, staying involved in the team despite his absence from the court.

    Led by Dosunmu and LaMelo Ball, Minnesota is presently fourth in the Western Conference with a 11-4 record and a pretty favorable schedule over the next few weeks.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:46PM EST.

    Universal Technical Institute (UTI -8.48%) released its final set of earnings for its 2026 fiscal year, and probably wishes it hadn't. The vocational education specialist fell short of analyst estimates, and its guidance also left something to be desired. Investors expressed their displeasure by trading the stock down by almost 9% that day.

    After market close on Wednesday, UTI revealed that its fourth-quarter revenue was $235.9 million, up more than 6% year over year. That was on the back of a 6%-plus rise in the average number of full-time students over the year, to 26,251.

    Net income took a different trajectory, sliding by almost 4% to slightly over $18 million, or $0.32 per share.

    That top-line figure was slightly higher than the average analyst estimate of just under $235 million. Pundits tracking UTI stock were also modeling a slightly higher earnings per share (EPS) figure of $0.33.

    Industry observers note that UTI is in the midst of implementing its multi-year "North Star Strategy," aimed at transforming its historical focus on training for certain vocations into a learning institute for a variety of them. It attributed the dip in profitability to expenses related to this effort.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    UTI also proffered revenue guidance for the current fiscal year of $925 million to $945 million.

    Industry observers note that however, those expenses -- which include spending on four planned upcoming campus openings -- will continue to impact the bottom line. Management is guiding for annual net income of $0 to $5 million ($0 to $0.09 per share), which would be well down from fiscal 2026's $33.6 million. It's also notably below the $0.73-per-share consensus analyst estimate (ditto for UTI's revenue guidance, which whiffs on the $971 million collective pundit forecast).

    It has been revealed that UTI's expansion plans are ambitious and, in my view, achievable. Demand for vocational education is high given the shortage of skilled professionals in such trades, so this feels like the opportune time to build out an educational business. I think UTI has a brighter future than the Thursday market reaction would indicate.

    The S&P 500 Just Fell 4 Straight Weeks From a Record High. Here’s Why I’m Buying the Dip.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.02%) closed at a record 7,818.93 on Oct.
    • Recent findings suggest that as of now, the index is about 8% below its October high.
    • But if you go back several decades and look at situations like this -- the S&P 500 declining four straight weeks following a record high -- the outlook from here could actually be pretty bullish.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:50PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    In a recent development, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.02%) closed at a record 7,818.93 on Oct. 6. It finished that week higher, but from there it closed lower four weeks in a row, culminating in its post-election day drubbing.

    Recent findings suggest that as of now, the index is about 8% below its October high. The Nasdaq-100 and the tech sector are faring far worse, and investors are thinking about a potential bear market for the first time in over a year.

    But if you go back several decades and look at situations like this -- the S&P 500 declining four straight weeks following a record high -- the outlook from here could actually be pretty bullish.

    In a recent development, since 1970, there have been 12 occasions when the S&P 500 has fallen four straight weeks right after hitting a latest all-time closing high the previous week. Historically, the short term following these events has been more volatile. But it's the longer-term recovery period that's more meaningful.

    According to recent reports, six months after the streak ended, the S&P 500 was higher in 10 of those 12 instances. The median gain was 13.4%, which is more than double the 5.2% median six-month gain during an average week since 1970.

    Over the subsequent 12 months, the S&P 500 was higher on 11 of the 12 occasions, with a median gain of 16.5%.

    I don't want to over-inflate the success rate here when the sample size is only 12, but I believe there's an explanation for this. Even bull markets have periods when stocks pull back. In many cases, it's not necessarily a sign that economic growth is stalling and a major bear market is imminent. It's just a normal part of the process of investing in risky assets. These are often normal market gyrations, and I think the data demonstrates that over the long term, stocks tend to rise more often than fall.

    Data source: Investing.com data and author's analysis of S&P 500 daily closing prices. "Streak ended" is the final trading day of the fourth losing week. Returns are measured from that close. Three months = 13 weeks; six months = 26 weeks; 12 months = 52 weeks.

    One month from the streak's end, the chances of a positive return are pretty much a coin flip. It's not until three months out that, historically at least, the odds start to swing in your favor.

    But I believe the overall trend is pretty clear and a good example of why a long-term buy-and-hold strategy is usually the best approach. In this scenario, the odds of generating a positive return have historically kept improving the longer you stay invested. That's a good framework to keep in mind whether stocks are steadily declining or near all-time highs.

    History suggests that dips like these are much more likely to be healthy pullbacks during longer-term rising markets than a bear market warning.

    It has been revealed that therefore, there's probably little need to make any major changes to your investment process. That means keeping your stock/bond allocations intact. Continue investing monthly or with every paycheck. Make sure your portfolio still aligns with your long-term goals.

    If anything, you could consider positioning the equity segment of your portfolio a little more defensively. Moving from a core position in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -1.98%) to something like the Vanguard Value ETF (VTV -1.58%) or the Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF (SPLV -1.27%) could be a smart way to take some risk off the table while maintaining your equity exposure.

    Market dips don't necessarily need to be feared. They can also be taken advantage of.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has reportedly been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
    • The recovery timetable for that injury is one to three weeks, depending on how Harper's rehabilitation progresses, according to Charania.
    • Harper, 20, sustained the injury during the Spurs' 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has reportedly been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.

    The recovery timetable for that injury is one to three weeks, depending on how Harper's rehabilitation progresses, according to Charania.

    Harper, 20, sustained the injury during the Spurs' 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday. In the closing minute of the fourth quarter, Harper was about to receive a pass from Stephon Castle while matched up against Detroit's Ausar Thompson.

    However, Harper's right foot slipped on the court and caused him to stretch awkwardly. He stayed down on the floor while play continued on the other end of the court, appearing to grab at his left hip or groin area.

    Sources indicate that the second-year guard was eventually able to stand up and walk off the court with some assistance from teammate Keldon Johnson. But he was noticeably limping and in pain as he went to the locker room. Harper did not return to the game during the final 53 seconds.

    In a recent development, "It just looked like he slipped, obviously," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson told reporters afterward, via the San Antonio Express-News' Tom Orsborn. "So hoping for the best, but don't know anything yet.".

    San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper slipped and suffered a hip injury late in Tuesday's loss to the Detroit Pistons.

    Sources indicate that harper appeared at Thursday's shootaround with no noticeable limp, according to Orsborn. But that was apparently before imaging results came back from the team's medical staff.

    Sources indicate that "I'm happy he's not as hurt as he could be," noted Spurs forward Julian Champagnie, who will replace Harper in the starting lineup. "Obviously, we need him, so finding out it wasn't that serious, or as serious as it could have been, was good news.".

    In a recent development, in 15 games this season, Harper is scoring 18.4 points per game, second on San Antonio behind Victor Wembanyama. He's also averaging 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists. He's shooting 50% from the floor and 31% on 54 3-point attempts.

    At 12-3, the Spurs are a half-game behind the Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the NBA's top record. San Antonio hosts the Los Angeles Clippers (4-9) on Thursday night, then has two days off before hosting the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans (5-11) on Saturday.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's a line uttered by actor Nicolas Cage as he portrays the eponymous protagonist in "Madden." Unfortunately, he's central to a movie that fails to live up to that credo and doesn't seem to have much Commitment to Excellence in its bid to depict Pro Football Hall of Famer John Madden.

    The movie, which began streaming on Prime Video on Wednesday, Nov. 18, opens with a black title card, which says, "Not all of this happened ... but most of it is true.".

    In a recent development, that effectively sets a tone for a movie that lacks drama, and − yep, authenticity. And while that might merely describes this movie's issues in broad brush strokes, "Madden" really flops for these five reasons:.

    While you might not think the 62-year-old Oscar winner would be a natural choice to play Madden, Cage put on 25 pounds and supplemented his weight gain with another 30 or so pounds of prosthetics to achieve something of a physical resemblance to the portly coach of the Oakland Raiders, TV analyst and entrepreneur.

    Yet Cage's creative direction is baffling. He commits to his version of Madden's voice, but he sounds nothing like the man − to the point of distraction. But that's hardly the most jarring aspect of his performance.

    Industry observers note that regardless of whatever phase of his career he was in, Madden was always an outsized character. And while he might have bordered on cartoonish as a coach, pitchman or, certainly at times, in the broadcast booth, he was nothing if not genuine and inimitable − plus brilliant in his various capacities. But Cage gives a rendition that's more a buffoonish caricature of an inattentive family man who dreams up football schemes with his head in a refrigerator (don't we all).

    Anyone who draws a first impression of Madden, imperfections and all, from this movie isn't likely to form an image of the man described by his players, colleagues, friends and family through the decades.

    Industry observers note that A disservice to his memory? You decide.

    According to recent reports, david O. Russell directed "Madden," though NFL Films was involved with the project − and football aficionados will certainly recognize some vintage football sequences intercut into the film.

    According to recent reports, otherwise? If you're not a football fan, "Madden" isn't likely to make you one.

    The movie essentially starts with the 1976 AFC Championship Game, during which Madden's Raiders were poised to finally vanquish their archnemeses, the Pittsburgh Steelers, after years of falling short to the 1970s' preeminent dynasty. But in a failed bid to interject some sense of drama, the Steelers score first in "Madden," even though they never actually led in a game Oakland won 24-7 in reality. And while there's some acknowledgement of the tension that existed at the time between these franchises, "Madden" doesn't attempt to illustrate the backstory of Oakland's failures against the Steelers, including the "Immaculate Reception," Pittsburgh coach Chuck Noll suggesting there was a "criminal element" to the Raiders, nor is there much exploration of the colorful characters on both teams.

    You might also come away thinking all football games are played inside stadiums with high concrete walls covered in bunting. Snippets of Cage using a telestrator? As silly as you might imagine. And scenes of actors playing football aren't value-added in the least − no reason to try and improve on NFL Films' capture of Hall of Famer Willie Brown's 75-yard pick-six in the Raiders' Super Bowl 11 blowout of the Minnesota Vikings, Madden's crowning achievement as a coach ... not that the point is driven home all that well in the movie.

    Snoop Dogg and former NFL stars Marshawn Lynch and Julian Edelman appear in "Madden." None do much more than serve as set pieces, Snoop the only one to even get a few lines − those serving to convey the cultural phenomenon that is EA Sports' "Madden NFL," which Madden himself was instrumental in developing, marketing and legitimizing.

    Industry observers note that seems like a squandered opportunity given the outsized personalities of this trio ... and, if I'm being honest, I didn't even realize Edelman was in the movie at all until I scanned the closing credits.

    WORST SPORTS MOVIES: Will 'Madden' join their ranks?

    Leave it to Batman to steal the show.

    But Christian Bale's depiction of Raiders owner Al Davis really stands out in this flick. Bale managed to replicate Davis' distinctive look, through various times in his life, as well as his signature Brooklyn accent. His relationship with his wife, Carol (played by Sienna Miller), comes across as far richer and more nuanced than Madden and his wife, Virginia − though Kathryn Hahn does a nice job in the role.

    But watching Bale as the recalcitrant, paranoid, renegade boss of the Raiders − and Madden's lifelong friend, despite the strain football often put on their relationship − leaves the viewer wanting for more, especially since Davis' football legacy is equally impactful to Madden's if not as well known or understood in pop culture.

    You'd think a movie about a larger-than-life persona like Madden's would be entertaining, at least largely so. Not the case here. "Madden" literally put me to sleep for 20 minutes even though its run time comes in shy of two hours. You'd think it would lend itself to humor. But that winds up being quite forced − whether it's Cage puking while battling an ulcer, Shane Gillis' fictional character Vince McGary as Madden's neighbor, or Cage and Bale listening to N.W.A. on the Madden Cruiser ... which hardly seems to serve a purpose and certainly doesn't much illustrate the Raiders' ethos, especially when they were based in Los Angeles at the time the hip-hop super group rose to prominence.

    Want a gripping, accurate feel for John Madden? I'd point you to Fox's documentary "All Madden.," which premiered on Christmas Day 2021, just days before Madden's death.

    Thankfully, that's the one the man himself got to see.

    This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Five reasons why 'Madden' movie fails miserably | Opinion.

    Sources indicate that on Nov. 17, shares of Walt Disney (DIS -1.72%) ended the day down 1.5%. This was despite the business reporting financial results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter (ended Oct. 3) that easily beat Wall Street estimates.

    It has been revealed that revenue totaled $25.9 billion, rising 16% year over year. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.77 was 59% higher compared to Q4 2025. Management guided this profit metric to grow in the double digits in fiscal 2027.

    What’s more, Disney showed its commitment to shareholders by boosting the annual dividend by 33% to $2 per share. And stock buybacks will total $9 billion over the coming fiscal year.

    Sources indicate that these are all encouraging signs at the House of Mouse. Here's what the latest results mean for investors.

    Recent findings suggest that the latest results show healthy financial performance for a business that has been navigating a changing media landscape amid the decline of cable TV. Entertainment streaming video-on-demand (SVOD), which includes Disney+ and Hulu (excluding live TV), has become a real profit engine. Its operating income jumped 97% in fiscal 2027, with a 13.6% Q4 operating margin.

    The downside, however, is a potential red flag regarding transparency. SVOD operating income will no longer be broken out starting with the current quarter's financial update.

    The experiences segment is the bright spot. It's the primary financial contributor to the overall business. Revenue and operating income increased by 15% and 20%, respectively, in Q4. Domestic parks attendance (up 11%) was a positive development.

    Recent findings suggest that capital expenditures will come in at $9 billion this fiscal year. It's mostly going toward bolstering parks and cruises. Disney's Avengers Campus in California, for example, will double in size in 2028, among other enhancements.

    According to recent reports, capital returns remain a priority for the leadership team after investing in strategic initiatives. A 33% dividend hike is a major announcement. And Disney will also conduct $9 billion in share buybacks in fiscal 2027. This is an indication of strong financial health. Free cash flow is expected to total $11 billion next fiscal year.

    The business told shareholders it plans to achieve annualized run rate cost savings of $3 billion by fiscal year 2029. "While these efficiencies will be used primarily to fund future growth, we do expect a portion to drop to the bottom line over time," the shareholder letter reads.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    It has been revealed that with adjusted EPS rising 18% year over year in fiscal 2026, Disney has now reported three straight years of strong double-digit profit growth. And its forecast calls for the trend to continue in fiscal 2027.

    According to recent reports, the momentum is worth highlighting. It's encouraging to see the manufacturer operate from a position of fundamental strength after years of questions about how it will navigate a streaming future.

    This positive trend isn't making shareholders happy, though. It's going in one ear and coming out the other. In the last three years, Disney's stock price has risen 30%. It's down 22% in five years. Investors would've made a lot more money if they owned an S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.02%) exchange-traded fund.

    It has been revealed that disney shares at the moment trade at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 15.8, well below the overall market. From a competitive standpoint, no other firm can replicate what Disney offers, which should command more positive market sentiment.

    Sources indicate that but I think the market is hesitant to assign a higher valuation multiple to the shares because the business requires significant capital to run and grow. Disney is in the middle of a 10-year, $60 billion investment cycle to spruce up its experiences division. And because of its huge presence in sports programming, valuable rights that certainly don't come cheap, it will spend $26 billion in cash just on content in fiscal 2027.

    It has been revealed that the stock has risen 20% over the past four months (as of Nov. 17). It's still worth taking a closer look at. Just don't count on market-crushing gains from here.

    Recent findings suggest that unknown Analyst: Okay. And then could you provide the split? You didn't break out cash taxes or working capital?

    IBM Stock Is Down About 23% in 2026. Here's Where I Think It Will Be in 2030.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than International Business Machines ›.
    • Sources indicate that my best estimate for International Business Machines (IBM -2.04%) is a share price of about $300 when 2030 ends.
    • I get there by multiplying the non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share I think IBM can earn in 2030, about $16.75, by 18 -- a price-to-earnings ratio in line with the stock's own history.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:04PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than International Business Machines ›.

    Sources indicate that my best estimate for International Business Machines (IBM -2.04%) is a share price of about $300 when 2030 ends. From roughly $227 as I write, that comes to a rise of about 32%, or about 7% a year before dividends.

    I get there by multiplying the non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share I think IBM can earn in 2030, about $16.75, by 18 -- a price-to-earnings ratio in line with the stock's own history.

    Even $300 is below the June 2 record close of $329.23. Shares today trade around 31% under that high, and they're down about 23% in 2026.

    In a recent development, most of this estimate depends on IBM's software business. For the third quarter, the segment made up around 46% of IBM's $17.1 billion in revenue but about 65% of its segment profit (the profit IBM reports for each business line).

    Showing how much the business has bounced back, software revenue grew 9% year over year in constant currency (a measure that removes exchange-rate moves) in the third quarter. This was a big acceleration from 5% in the second quarter. And the second quarter had itself marked a slowdown from 8% in the first quarter and 11% in the fourth quarter of 2025. Better yet, software's segment profit margin improved to 35% from 33% a year before, so the segment is keeping more profit per dollar of sales.

    In January, management expected software to grow around 10% this year. On IBM's Oct. 21 earnings call, CFO Jim Kavanaugh remarked the firm now sees around 7% to 8%, with 7% as the base case.

    But IBM's annual recurring revenue, a yearly run rate for its recurring software business, rose 8% to $24.9 billion in the third quarter. And Kavanaugh noted he expects the growth rate to approach double digits in the fourth quarter.

    According to recent reports, IBM's adjusted earnings per share reached $11.59 in 2025, up 12% from 2024. So far in 2026, through September, they've risen around 10% to $7.79. Quarterly growth moved from 19% to 5% to 11% -- the same drop and rebound software went through.

    If fourth-quarter earnings per share just equal last year's $4.52, IBM would end 2026 at around $12.31.

    From there, I assume earnings per share climb around 8% a year, hitting about $16.75 in 2030. That's slower than the last two years, mostly because the rest of IBM grows more slowly than software. Consulting, its second-biggest segment, grew just 2% at constant currency in the third quarter. Also, IBM's diluted share count ticked up in the last year, to around 954 million, so buybacks aren't doing much for earnings per share.

    When 2022 ended, IBM stock traded at around 15 times earnings, using that year's adjusted earnings per share. The ratio climbed to about 17 times earnings by the close of 2023, then to 21 times earnings a year later and 26 times earnings by the end of 2025.

    At the June record, shares cost around 28 times adjusted earnings for the previous four quarters.

    Industry observers note that now IBM stock goes for about 18 times the adjusted earnings it posted in the last year, and about 17 times analysts' average earnings forecast for 2027. So shares arguably sit toward the low end of their recent range already.

    Sources indicate that I pick 18 times earnings for 2030 -- close to today's price-to-earnings ratio and under the average of the four year-ends, about 20 times earnings. Applied to about $16.75 in earnings per share, this gives a stock price near $300.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    Of course, software might move the result either way. If it gets back to the 10% growth IBM expected in January and earnings per share gain about 10% a year, the stock could hit about $325 at the same valuation.

    But if software settles near the second quarter's 5% rate and investors pay 15 times earnings, like they did at the end of 2022, shares might finish 2030 about where they are now.

    IBM, which has paid dividends every year since 1916, also pays $1.69 a share each quarter, a yield of around 3% at today's price. Add it to about 7% a year from price gains, and my estimate suggests a total return of about 10% a year through 2030.

    In a recent development, that's not a stellar return, but I think it's a good one for a company whose most profitable segment is growing faster again. I'd be comfortable buying IBM shares near today's price.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:26PM EST.
    • According to recent reports, for more aggressive growth investors, Tilray Brands (TLRY -8.00%) appears to be moving in a positive direction as a business.
    • Industry observers note that when Tilray first went public, its goal was to take advantage of the increasing legal access to cannabis.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:26PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tilray Brands ›.

    According to recent reports, for more aggressive growth investors, Tilray Brands (TLRY -8.00%) appears to be moving in a positive direction as a business. It may be worth buying if you have a long time horizon. However, more conservative investors will probably want to remain on the sidelines because the company still hasn't achieved one crucial goal: sustainable profitability. Here's why this financially strong cannabis seller is worth buying for some investors, but not for others.

    Industry observers note that when Tilray first went public, its goal was to take advantage of the increasing legal access to cannabis. There was significant excitement in the market around the marijuana sector at the time, and the stock rose sharply alongside the rest of the sector. But the reality didn't live up to Wall Street's expectations. Competition was intense, the legalization trend was slow, and illicit marijuana sales remained robust. Tilray and the rest of the sector fell sharply.

    Industry observers note that tilray decided to move in a different direction. The goal now is to be a "global lifestyle and consumer packaged goods tech giant leading at the nexus of the beverage, cannabis, and wellness industries." Effectively, the company is looking to operate more like a consumer staples company than a pure-play cannabis business. The biggest shift was the acquisition of alcoholic beverage brands.

    In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues from Tilray's alcoholic beverages stood at $101.5 million, while its cannabis revenues totaled $56.1 million. You could easily argue that Tilray is now more of an alcohol firm than a marijuana company. However, the bigger story is the diversification that the company has created. That should attract growth investors who want exposure to cannabis, but who don't want to own a pure-play cannabis company.

    The truth is, marijuana is a growing industry. The problem is that companies have had a hard time translating that growth into profits. Tilray is looking to resolve that problem by diversifying into fresh areas that have a more stable history, notably craft brewing. That creates a foundation on which it can continue to build its marijuana operations.

    That foundation, meanwhile, is increasingly strong. Notably, it ended the first fiscal quarter of 2027 with a net cash position. That requires a little parsing, because it means the firm's cash balance of roughly $215 million exceeds its long-term debt of $118 million. That's not quite as good as a debt-free balance sheet, but Tilray has a very strong financial position right at the moment.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, the company's growth in Europe has been a strong point, further adding to its diversification. In the first quarter, European revenues increased by 71%. From a high-level perspective, Tilray is a much stronger business today than it was not that long ago. If you are a growth investor with a long-term focus, you may want to take a closer look. It could be a good way to add marijuana exposure without having to own a pure-play.

    Recent findings suggest that while there is a lot to like about Tilray and the direction the business is moving, there's one key issue that remains unresolved. Tilray continues to bleed red ink on the bottom line. That single fact should probably keep more conservative investors on the sidelines. The direction the business is heading looks good, but until there are sustainable profits, an investment here remains a risky one. Buying it requires believing that Tilray's consumer-staples shift will eventually lead to a profitable and growing business. Only a more aggressive growth investor will likely be willing to make that bet.

    Nvidia Just Raised Its Supply Commitments to $390 Billion, Mostly for Memory. Micron Is the Memory Stock I'd Buy.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that when Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) reported on Nov.
    • Sources indicate that nvidia's supply commitments rose to $390 billion, up from $279 billion a quarter earlier.
    • Industry observers note that that's good news for Micron Technology (MU -2.10%), one of the three big makers of the memory chips Nvidia buys.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 19, 2026 at 11:07PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Sources indicate that when Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) reported on Nov. 17, its fiscal third-quarter revenue had more than doubled from the year before, to a record $115.8 billion. But for memory investors, the more telling number was how much the artificial intelligence (AI) chip leader has agreed to pay its suppliers.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's supply commitments rose to $390 billion, up from $279 billion a quarter earlier. And the company stated the increase was "primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply.".

    Industry observers note that that's good news for Micron Technology (MU -2.10%), one of the three big makers of the memory chips Nvidia buys. But Micron stock is around $702 as I write, about 42% under the record $1,213.56 it closed at on June 25.

    I think the market's underrating what Nvidia's report notes about Micron's business.

    Showing how fast its buying has picked up, Nvidia's supply commitments have more than tripled over two quarters. They were at $119 billion as of April 26, climbed to $279 billion by July 26, and hit $390 billion by Oct. 25, the end of its fiscal third quarter. In both of the last two quarters, the firm linked most of the rise to memory. What's more, the money's coming due sooner. Of the $390 billion, $203 billion falls in Nvidia's fiscal 2028, which ends in January 2028. Three months earlier, that year's figure was $87 billion.

    In short, Nvidia is locking in memory long before it needs the chips, and much of this spending will probably land within about a year.

    Nvidia doesn't say how it splits the spending between its memory suppliers. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics sell Nvidia high-bandwidth memory (HBM), too. (HBM is the stacked memory that sits next to AI processors.).

    Micron doesn't name its largest buyers, either. However, no single customer made up 10% or more of its revenue for its fiscal 2026, which ended Sept. 3, down from one customer at 17% the year before.

    So Micron's direct sales to Nvidia, whatever they are, were under a tenth of its revenue last year.

    Industry observers note that what Micron does say is encouraging. It's working with Nvidia on what it calls the industry's first custom HBM4E chip, designed for Nvidia's next generation of graphics processing units.

    Sources indicate that and its cloud memory business unit, which sells HBM to all data center customers, keeps growing. It pulled in $16.3 billion of revenue in the three months ended Sept. 3, up 18% from the previous quarter and more than triple the $4.5 billion of a year before, with an 83% gross margin. On its fiscal fourth-quarter call, Micron said it had lifted its HBM prices significantly for calendar 2027.

    Nvidia's commitments look like the buyer's side of a change Micron is already building its business around.

    In a recent development, micron has now signed 26 multiyear strategic customer agreements, up from 16 a quarter earlier. All are take-or-pay deals, so customers commit to buying fixed volumes and can lose deposits if they fall short.

    Customers have committed $32 billion under the deals, mainly as cash deposits, compared to the $22 billion Micron forecast a quarter before.

    Recent findings suggest that micron also puts its remaining performance obligations (contracted sales it hasn't recognized yet) at around $150 billion, counting just committed volumes at minimum prices. "[E]ven at floor prices, we expect margins meaningfully above any prior cycle peak margins," chief financial officer Mark Murphy noted in Micron's prepared remarks for the fiscal fourth quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    But the stock trades like the boom might end soon. At around $702, Micron's price-to-earnings ratio is about 4 based on analysts' estimates for fiscal 2027 (which ends next September), and only about 9 on fiscal 2026's actual earnings of $74.33 per share. A price like that suggests investors expect profits to dive before long.

    Sure, memory prices have crashed before, and Micron aims to spend more on fresh plant space, which might loosen supply in late 2028 and beyond. But a growing share of its sales now comes with committed volumes, deposits, and price floors, protections Micron didn't have in past memory busts.

    In a recent development, of the three companies selling Nvidia its memory, Micron is the one I'd buy. It's working with Nvidia on custom HBM, and unlike Samsung, it's a pure memory and storage business. At around 4 times expected earnings, the stock looks cheap to me even if Nvidia's money is split three ways.

    AI Token Prices Are Tumbling. Is It a Red Flag for Anthropic Stock?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic (ANT +17.07%) just finished its IPO day with the AI lab jumping 17% in its blockbuster debut.
    • Industry observers note that anthropic's debut exposes stock market investors to AI labs for the first time, and Anthropic may have a broader range of potential outcomes than any stock before it.
    • Likewise, Anthropic bulls, including Goldman Sachs, projected $440 billion in revenue by 2029, and Morningstar's bull case put its share price at $188.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 20, 2026 at 12:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +17.07%) just finished its IPO day with the AI lab jumping 17% in its blockbuster debut.

    Industry observers note that anthropic's debut exposes stock market investors to AI labs for the first time, and Anthropic may have a broader range of potential outcomes than any stock before it. The company has identified a market opportunity valued at $40 trillion, and its technology is so powerful that CEO Dario Amodei thinks it could cure diseases like cancer and Alzheimer's within a decade. In contrast, a researcher for the company remarked there's more than a 10% chance that it "could kill all humans.".

    Likewise, Anthropic bulls, including Goldman Sachs, projected $440 billion in revenue by 2029, and Morningstar's bull case put its share price at $188.

    Anthropic bears, on the other hand, have argued that the manufacturer doesn't have a sustainable competitive advantage and faces too much competition from cheaper models and the threat of distillation.

    Among the top critiques is that token prices are falling sharply, as Bloomberg's chief economist argues below.

    Recent findings suggest that in today’s piece @TheTerminal, I write about why Anthropic IPO may mark the end of the AI trade. https://t.co/BhCWhrbIbM Two charts summarized it the argument: 1) Its effective price per million token has come down sharply of late (its s-1 cutoff date gives financial statements up to 9/30) 2) yet its token usage share didn’t pick up, and even edged down That reveals the kind of market structure that it operates in. It seems to be an oligopolist who does not have durable pricing power. Growth has to rely on price cuts to drive volume. That is a tough business.

    The usage-weighted Silicon Data LLM Token Expenditure Index, which tracks prices per million tokens, fell more than 40% between early June 30 and early October, and prices have continued to fall since then.

    Anthropic has even cut its prices by 20% on its newest frontier model, Fable 5.2.

    Token prices are falling for a number of reasons. First, competition from cheaper models is pushing prices across the industry lower. Second, customers are shifting their consumption habits and using cheaper models for more routine tasks, and third, costs to generate tokens are falling due to more efficient computing usage, allowing Anthropic to lower prices without necessarily losing profit.

    The consequences of lower token prices aren't fully clear. Superficially, lower prices would seem to be bad, as it would lower Anthropic's revenue, but lower prices can also drive increased usage, a relationship known as the Jevons paradox, which is a benefit over the long term.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic's strong growth through the third quarter indicates that the firm can grow even while token prices are falling, as it reported 47% sequential growth in the third quarter. Additionally, the company has managed to scale revenue faster than its computing costs, resulting in an adjusted operating profit.

    Still, falling token prices could put pressure on Anthropic, especially if rising competition and usage shifts are driving them.

    Sources indicate that CEO Dario Amodei has called for a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, referring to a method of training AI models that uses existing models, rather than training on data from scratch. Distillation is comparable to counterfeiting in other industries. It lowers prices, but does so at the expense of undercutting the investment and research and development that market leaders have made, disincentivizing it in the long run. Amodei also sees it as a national security threat, as distillation allows China to build much better models than it normally would be able to.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    In technology, prices often fall over time due to competition and as the technology evolves and gets more efficient.

    Amazon invented cloud computing and remains the market leader, even though the firm has cut costs hundreds of times due to economies of scale, competitive pressure, and incentivizing customers to stay on its platform. AWS continues to grow and has become one of the most valuable businesses in the world, even on a stand-alone basis.

    Anthropic has a number of similarities to AWS as a leader in a latest technology with a massive addressable market ahead of it, and pricing is just one part of the equation.

    Demand for artificial intelligence could be nearly limitless, and investors shouldn't lose sight of that. While token prices are worth monitoring, if Anthropic can continue to grow profits, falling token prices aren't the red flag that bears seem to think they are.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that enterprise software and cloud infrastructure organization Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    Industry observers note that after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he mentioned.

    According to recent reports, "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," said DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    According to recent reports, while Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as fresh contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    DiFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

    It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space organization with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Recent findings suggest that gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

    "Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," noted Anmuth.

    Sources indicate that in the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst remarked. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

    Meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst stated. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

    While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

    Industry observers note that anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 20, 2026 at 1:10AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than iShares Trust - iShares Semiconductor ETF ›.

    Industry observers note that one of the hottest exchange-traded funds (ETFs) this year has been the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX -2.75%). This ETF, which tracks an index that features the 30 largest U.S. semiconductor stocks, has returned an impressive 37% this year and 49% over the past 12 months.

    According to recent reports, but since the recent peak of $196 per share on Oct. 6, the day the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -2.25%) reached an all-time high, the ETF has been in a downward spiral, with the price dropping about 30% to $138 per share at this writing.

    A combination of factors caused the meltdown, including overvalued large caps, concerns about overspending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, and negative sentiment toward building more data centers — particularly as Democrats swept into Congress.

    Also, the Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) scandal and the resignation of its longtime CEO Jensen Huang pulled down semiconductor and technology stocks pretty much across the board.

    So, it has been a rough couple of months for semiconductor stocks, but here's why I think the iShares Semiconductor ETF will have another strong year in 2027.

    Industry observers note that the sharp sell-off of semiconductor stocks should serve as a reset of sorts. The correction was overdue because many top chip stocks had become overvalued amid rapid growth over the past three to four years.

    This reset should bring their valuations down to more attractive, sustainable levels, potentially sparking a bounce-back rally in 2027.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    A slowdown in data center development is certainly on the table, if not likely, given that it was a major glitch in the recent election campaigns. That may have a longer-term impact, and it may not -- only time will tell. There just may be more restrictions and parameters on where data centers are located and how they operate.

    But it shouldn't have a major effect on chip stocks in 2027. Hyperscalers have a huge amount of backlog of contracts on the books waiting to be executed, and many chipmakers are already sold out of AI chips for 2027 and into 2028.

    According to recent reports, also, the supercycle created by the supply-demand imbalance among memory and storage stocks remains. Supply is not expected to catch up to demand for at least a few years, and that gives chipmakers huge pricing power. A potential slowdown in building AI data centers could help ease the supply-demand imbalance somewhat, but likely down the road beyond 2027.

    So, the correction in chip stocks might be painful right now, but I think it makes for a more attractive buying opportunity for the iShares Semiconductor ETF heading into 2027.
